newsitem.title: USA: US Spot Products-NYH reformulated gasoline slides.
newsitem.headline: US Spot Products-NYH reformulated gasoline slides.

text.p: New York Harbor reformulated gasoline differentials fell sharply by late Tuesday as one refiner sold a large parcel below prevailing prices.
Gulf Coast gasoline differentials held the gains made early in the day as buyers pushed upline prices for conventional barrels, according to traders.
On the NYMEX, July gasoline gained 0.20 cent to settle at 56.40 cents a gallon and July heating oil firmed 0.15 cent to end at 51.65 cents a gallon.
NEW YORK HARBOR
New York Harbor reformulated gasoline (RFG) values fell Tuesday as midcontinent refiner Koch Industries sold a barge below the futures price, knocking the differential into negative territory.
Koch sources confirmed the RFG sale at 0.25 cent under NYMEX July gasoline versus Monday's talk which pegged the offer at 0.20 cent above July gasoline.
"A2 just got hammered after the Koch deal," said a Harbor trader.
Still, the general market talk for RFG was above Koch's deal, with the prompt offer at even to July gasoline and the bid at 0.25 cent under.
Heating oil traded at 0.15 cent under July heat.
"I could have gotten a better price if I pushed harder," said the trader who did the deal, noting heating oil values have been steadying.
Sun Co posted it's price for heating oil earlier at 0.25 cent under. Low sulphur diesel was offered at 0.50 cent over July heating oil.
U.S. GULF COAST
Regular conventional M1 gasoline saw buying interest, especially in upline barrels on the Colonial Pipeline, traders said.
Those upline barrels changed hands at 1.00 cents under the July NYMEX gasoline, up from about 1.50 cents from their level in Houston on Monday. Traders said Exxon was the main buyer of those barrels.
Prompt M1 gasoline in Houston changed hands at 1.50 cents under the July NYMEX, about 0.25 cent up from the previous day, traders said, and helped by the upline firmness.

Prompt premium 93-octane D1 reformulated gasoline differentials firmed about 0.50 cent as barrels traded at 5.00 cents over the July NYMEX, and prompt premium 93-octane V1 conventional gasoline differentials gained 0.25 cent with a trade at 5.25 cents over the NYMEX.
"I think it's going to stay this way for a while," one player said, suggesting premium gasolines would see continue to see firmer differentials.
Low sulphur diesel differentials also firmed modestly, with prompt barrels trading at 1.50 cents under the July futures, up about 0.20 cent from Monday.
MIDCONTINENT

Unleaded gasoline differentials in the Midcontinent markets rose Tuesday following interest in prompt cash barrels. Group Three unleaded differentials rose a half cent this afternoon, building on a quarter cent gain this morning. Players said deals for 6.25 cents over the July NYMEX were done, and 6.50 cents over the print were also heard trading hands.
"There is not a lot of buying but one or two people were short," said a Group Three player.
Chicago unleaded differentials rose a quarter cent to 3.50 to 3.75 cents. Differentials for low sulphur and jet fuel in both hubs were talked steady.
-- New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1620
